candidates.label: Perge archaeological site
candidates.support: The extensively excavated site east of modern Antalya, per Wikidata 'an ancient city of Pamphylia,' is undisputed as ancient Perga; the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's coordinate for the site and Wikidata's coordinate agree closely.

summary.text: Perga was a major city of Pamphylia in southern Asia Minor. On the first missionary journey, Paul and Barnabas sailed to Perga from Paphos, and it was here that John Mark left the party and returned to Jerusalem; the pair passed back through Perga, preaching there, on their return journey before sailing home from Attalia.

history.text: Sources differ on Perga's province in about AD 50. The Roman historian Cassius Dio reports that in AD 43 Claudius incorporated the Lycians into the district of Pamphylia. The Roman historian Tacitus, however, records that under the Roman emperor Galba (AD 68-69) the provinces of Galatia and Pamphylia had a single governor, and other sources describe Pamphylia as part of Galatia until the Roman emperor Vespasian created the province of Lycia and Pamphylia after AD 70. This project follows the second view and places Perga in Galatia.

scripture.textWEB: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
But they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia. They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down.
When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
